title: Makefiles & Task Runners
description: Practical Make and task-runner reference covering dependency graphs, targets, prerequisites, recipes, variables, functions, pattern rules, automatic dependencies, phony and order-only targets, parallelism, recursive builds, shell behavior, portability, caching, CI, security, and task-runner selection.

subtopics.title: Targets, Prerequisites & Recipes
subtopics.description: Make updates a target when it is missing or older than a prerequisite, then runs its recipe. Declare the artifact graph rather than an unconditional sequence of shell commands.

codeBlocks.code:
build/app: cmd/app/main.go go.mod go.sum
	go build -o $@ ./cmd/app

.PHONY: build
build: build/app

callouts.title: Recipe Lines Require a Recipe Prefix
callouts.text: Traditionally this is a tab, not spaces. Editors can hide the difference; GNU Make can configure .RECIPEPREFIX, but portability may suffer.

subtopics.title: Default Goals, .PHONY & Force Targets
subtopics.description: The first ordinary target is the default goal unless overridden. Phony targets name actions, avoid collisions with files, and skip implicit-rule search.

codeBlocks.code:
.DEFAULT_GOAL := help

.PHONY: help test clean
help:
	@printf '%s\n' 'make test' 'make build'

test:
	go test ./...

clean:
	$(RM) -r build

callouts.title: Do Not Mark Real Artifacts Phony
callouts.text: A phony artifact rebuilds every invocation and prevents timestamp-based incremental behavior. Use phony only for action/group targets.

subtopics.title: Normal vs Order-Only Prerequisites
subtopics.description: Normal prerequisites affect both ordering and out-of-date checks; order-only prerequisites must exist/run first but their timestamps do not force rebuilds.

callouts.title: Directory Timestamps Change Often
callouts.text: Use an order-only directory prerequisite so adding another output file does not make every target depending on the directory rebuild.

subtopics.title: Variables, Assignment & Precedence
subtopics.description: Recursive = expands when used; simple := expands immediately; ?= sets only if undefined; += appends. Command-line variables normally override makefile assignments.

codeBlocks.code:
BUILD_DIR ?= build
SOURCES := $(wildcard src/*.c)
CPPFLAGS += -Iinclude
CFLAGS ?= -O2 -g

callouts.title: Environment and Make Variables Are Distinct Layers
callouts.text: Understand command line, override, makefile, and environment precedence. Export only variables child processes genuinely need.

subtopics.title: Pattern Rules & Automatic Variables
subtopics.description: Pattern rules generalize artifact transformations. Automatic variables describe the current target and prerequisites and are meaningful inside recipes.

codeBlocks.code:
build/%.o: src/%.c | build
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -MMD -MP -c $< -o $@

# $@ target, $< first prerequisite, $^ all normal prerequisites
-include $(OBJECTS:.o=.d)

callouts.title: Quote Shell Paths Where Possible
callouts.text: Make expands variables before the shell parses the recipe. Filenames with whitespace and metacharacters are difficult in many Make idioms; constrain project paths and avoid constructing commands from untrusted values.

subtopics.title: Functions, call, foreach & eval
subtopics.description: Built-in functions transform text and files. call creates parameterized macros; eval parses generated makefile syntax and expands twice, making it powerful but hard to debug.

codeBlocks.code:
comma := ,
empty :=
space := $(empty) $(empty)
packages := api worker

define test_package
.PHONY: test-$(1)
test-$(1):
	go test ./cmd/$(1)/...
endef
$(foreach pkg,$(packages),$(eval $(call test_package,$(pkg))))

callouts.title: Prefer Explicit Rules to Clever Metaprogramming
callouts.text: Generated make syntax can obscure dependency edges and expansion timing. Use it only when it removes substantial repetitive structure and add tests/debug output.

subtopics.title: Recipe Shells, Lines & Error Handling
subtopics.description: By default each logical recipe line runs in a separate shell. Use line continuations or .ONESHELL deliberately, and make failure behavior explicit.

callouts.title: Dollar Signs Have Two Expansion Stages
callouts.text: Use $ for Make variables and $$ when the shell must receive a dollar sign. Review command echo carefully for secrets.

subtopics.title: Parallel Builds & Recursive Make
subtopics.description: make -j runs independent targets concurrently. Correct parallelism requires complete dependencies and recipes that do not race on shared outputs or temporary files.

callouts.title: Use $(MAKE), Not make, Recursively
callouts.text: The special variable propagates jobserver and command-line behavior. Prefer one non-recursive graph where practical; recursive boundaries can hide cross-project dependencies.

subtopics.title: GNU vs POSIX Make & Reproducibility
subtopics.description: GNU Make extensions improve ergonomics but do not work in every make. Declare the required implementation, pin toolchains, and ensure outputs depend on all material inputs.

codeBlocks.code:
Declare: GNU Make >= supported version or POSIX-only policy
Pin: compiler/runtime/package manager/container image
Inputs: sources, generated config, lockfiles, environment/tool versions
Outputs: deterministic paths/content where feasible
CI: clean build + incremental build + parallel build

callouts.title: Timestamps Are an Approximation of Content Change
callouts.text: Generated files, clock skew, restored archives, and undeclared environment inputs can fool timestamp logic. Use content-addressed build systems when stronger reproducibility/scale is required.

subtopics.title: Make vs just, Task, npm Scripts & Build Systems
subtopics.description: Choose based on whether work is an artifact dependency graph, command catalog, language package lifecycle, or hermetic distributed build.

callouts.title: One Front Door Can Call Specialized Tools
callouts.text: A small Makefile/runner may expose consistent commands while Maven, Cargo, npm, Gradle, or another build system owns its native dependency graph.

subtopics.title: CI Integration, Secrets & Untrusted Input
subtopics.description: CI should invoke the same deterministic targets as developers while credentials, release mutations, and environment selection remain protected explicit steps.

codeBlocks.code:
.PHONY: ci
ci: format-check lint test build

.PHONY: release-check
release-check: ci
	./scripts/verify-clean-tree
	./scripts/inspect-package

callouts.title: Makefiles Execute Code
callouts.text: Review included makefiles, shell expansions, downloaded tools, and pull-request workflows. Never pass untrusted branch, path, or version text into eval or shell commands without strict validation.

subtopics.title: Debugging & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Inspect make's database and expansion, use dry runs carefully, keep targets small, document inputs/outputs, and test clean, incremental, parallel, and failed builds.

codeBlocks.code:
make -n target          # dry-run; recursive recipes may still behave specially
make --warn-undefined-variables target
make --debug=v target
make -pRrq : 2>/dev/null  # inspect database with care

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Declare tool/shell requirements, model real dependencies, mark only actions phony, use order-only prerequisites, generate dependency files, support parallelism, avoid hidden environment inputs, pin tools, protect release credentials, and test clean/incremental/failure behavior.
